newsitem.title: UK: UK power market liberalisation costs could double.
newsitem.headline: UK power market liberalisation costs could double.

text.p: Costs to British domestic customers of liberalising the electricity market could be over two pounds a head per year but should be outweighed by competition savings, Stephen Littlechild, head of industry watchdog Offer, said.

"It might be of the order of double (earlier one pound per year estimates), but we think the benefits more than outweigh that," Littlechild told parliament's trade and industry select committee on Wednesday.

Offer has estimated costs of implementing plans for liberalising the market from April 1998 at around 210 million pounds along with 50 million pounds for changes at the wholesale market or pool, or around one pound a year on average bills.
But the committee heard that East Midlands Electricity had estimated that the cost to the industry could be as high as 500 million pounds.
Littlechild said at that level, costs to customers would double but added that Offer would not accept these estimates at face value.
"We need to look again at these latest estimates and see if there are any grounds for increasing the impact on customers," he said.

He said that lower costs of generation bought by companies, which account for around 50 percent of domestic bills, would help to cut prices and that costs of the supply business, which make up 6-10 percent of bills, should also decrease.

Regional electricity companies (Recs) currently paying around 13 percent premiums to pool prices for some contracts, could see those reduced, possibly to around five percent, as competition gets underway, Littlechild suggested.
"I believe there will be lower prices as a result of keener purchasing," Littlechild said.
"We shall certainly be giving (companies) some guidance" on what costs can be passed on to customers, Littlechild said.
The electricity market is due to be freed up entirely to competition from April 1998 while domestic bills are currently subject to price controls set by Offer.
